findings.summary: intent_digest omitted session_ref and agent_runtime, so the same key sent to another session or runtime was answered as a REPLAY. Snapshot C closes this at LOCAL: target, runtime and principal are in the digest, all three axes return CONFLICT, and no/expired context and self-asserted principal are refused.

The observation-to-SETTLED judgment was not wired into the production path and the write entry could self-attest. Snapshot D closes the effect-safety half at LOCAL with a red->green control: D3, D4 and D10 are closed and regressions D1/D2/D5-D9/D11-D14 hold. The residual is P1: owner-observation reconcile still has no production caller.

E5: the S1 pair is individually green but NOT authoritatively joined at send admission. agent.binding.record accepts a caller-forged writer (EVIL/999), then LocalLoopbackTransport sends ADMITTED even though the live Work Engine lease on the same resource is held by a different owner/token (A/1). held_leases is not on the send path. Exit 1: 22 held, 1 SECURITY_FAIL.

D3 cross-actor forgery: another trusted actor could settle A's attempt using A's copied digest and a fabricated result. Snapshot D closes this at LOCAL: the write is refused UNTRUSTED_ACTOR and the attempt is unchanged.

D4 terminal-state regression: a terminal SETTLED could be written back to CALL_NOT_SENT, after which the kernel returns PROCEED, so a retry becomes a second effect. Snapshot D closes this at LOCAL: an authentic SETTLED cannot move to CALL_NOT_SENT or EFFECT_UNKNOWN, EFFECT_UNKNOWN cannot move back, and a terminal retry is REPLAY.
